summary.headline: Alembic Q4 FY26 revenue rose 4% YoY to INR1,838 crore; FY27 guided to low double-digit consolidated top-line growth with Pivya launch drag of 100-150 bps.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR1,838 crore, up 4% YoY, with core EBITDA margin near 25% (vs 24%) and gross margin at 71%. Reported PAT was INR203 crore, helped by a one-time INR101 crore tax adjustment, after a INR24 crore exceptional item. R&D rose to INR209 crore (11% of revenue) on peptide development and higher filings. For FY26, revenue grew about 10%, EBITDA before R&D was INR1,846 crore (25% of revenue), and reported PAT grew 16% to INR675 crore. Management guided FY27 to low double-digit consolidated growth, with R&D of INR750-800 crore and capex of INR300-350 crore.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR151 crore (9%) in Q4 FY25
includes INR24 crore exceptional item and INR101 crore one-time tax positive adjustment
+~INR50 crore vs December quarter, mainly receivables not yet due

segments.name: India business
segments.commentary: Q4 growth of 4% YoY led by price and new launches; full-year growth 5%. Specialty therapies (gynecology, gastroenterology, ophthalmology) and animal health outperformed; focus brands grew ahead of portfolio.

segments.name: US generics and international
segments.commentary: US grew in Q4 on volumes and six new launches during the quarter. Ex-US grew 20% for FY26 but was muted in Q4 on a high base and one-offs.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Modest Q4 growth driven by volumes, with pricing a headwind. Management said API prices are holding at premium levels and solvent cost increases have not yet been passed on, absorbed by inventory.

segments.name: US branded (Alembic Therapeutics, Pivya)
segments.commentary: Started operations in Q4 with Pivya launched in February 2026 for UTI, with a small field force targeting high-prescription territories. Management estimates a 100-150 bps margin drag from this business in FY27, expected to turn around by year-end.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated top-line growth guided to low double-digit percentage; management said no guidance is given on EBITDA margin numbers.
Management expects core margin improvement to cover the Pivya launch drag, with margins improving in FY27 and a return toward ~20% EBITDA margin over 2-3 years.
FY27 segment view: US business 10-15% growth in INR terms; ROW (international generics) 15%-plus; API closer to 10% (high single to low double digit); India to approach market growth.
R&D spend guided at INR750-800 crore for FY27, about 8-9% of revenue, down from 11% in Q4.
Capex guided at INR300-350 crore for FY27, mainly capacity, debottlenecking and replacement; peptide capex already completed and branded business needs no capex.
Management expects one or two more quarters of Pivya drag, with a meaningful contribution from the branded business expected toward year-end.
capex_capacity: Indore facility is fully operational; capacity utilization improving, supporting supply reliability and efficiency.
F3 ophthalmic line is at full capacity and is being expanded; F3's other two lines run at about 40% and 60% utilization.

F2 injectable and OSD lines are running at a decent level, with limited competition opportunities expected to lift utilization; some contract manufacturing and licensing is already in progress and should contribute in FY27.

Peptide capex is complete and was done within an existing API facility, with no dedicated capex disclosed; formulation runs on existing capacity. Five to six peptide products are in the pipeline, two filed.
FY27 capex guided at INR300-350 crore.
demand_pricing: API pricing remains a headwind, but management says Alembic sells at premium prices and does not compete at the bottom of the market.
Solvent prices are rising, but the company is using higher inventory and has not yet passed costs on; management says this has not affected margins.
Management is not assuming any easing in pricing pressure, competition or supply chain volatility in FY27.
Development costs are rising as competition increases, lowering the threshold IRR for R&D projects, though some opportunities remain.
Pivya early trends are described as healthy, but the company is not yet sharing prescription data.

qa_highlights.question: How much cost do the underutilized F2 and F3 facilities add each year, and when will they cover their costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not give a facility-wise breakup. F3 ophthalmic is at full capacity and being expanded, and the F2 and F3 lines are running at higher occupancy; the unabsorbed cost is described as small, and some contract manufacturing and licensing is already in progress for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much drag is Pivya putting on margins, and how long will it last?
qa_highlights.answer: No product-level number is given. Management says to model 100-150 bps of drag from the US branded business, with one or two more quarters of drag and a turnaround expected in the last quarter of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R&D productivity measure given the step-up in spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says Q4 at 11% of revenue was an outlier from complex and peptide development; FY27 R&D is expected at INR750-odd crore, about 8-9% of revenue. Projects are assessed by IRR, and the threshold IRR has fallen as competition raises development costs.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 EBITDA margin expected to improve over FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the margin should improve this year as the Pivya drag ends and core business growth offsets it. It gave no numeric margin guidance and said the first couple of quarters will show more.

qa_highlights.question: What is the implied US growth in constant currency?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed with the framing that 10-15% INR growth implies about 7-8% in constant currency, but said this is a view and not formal guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Where will capital be allocated in FY27-28 beyond peptides?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is largely complete. Focus is on in-licensing more branded products for Alembic Therapeutics and on measured R&D spend in complex products.

risks_watch: Pivya launch drag of 100-150 bps on margins for one or two more quarters, with the branded business still early and no prescription data disclosed.
R&D spend at INR750-800 crore for FY27 against the 8-9% of revenue target, with uncertain returns from earlier peptide and late-expiry filings.
Solvent cost inflation not yet passed on to API customers, with inventory cover expected to shield margins only for the near term.
Ongoing pricing pressure in API and India, with India guided only to approach market growth.
Full-year FY26 PAT growth was helped by a one-time INR101 crore tax benefit, so underlying profit growth is lower than reported.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term direction and core-business recovery, but cautious on near-term numbers: management declined to give FY27 margin or Pivya metrics and called FY27 directional. Evasive on the F2/F3 unabsorbed cost and on IRR-based R&D returns, which it did not quantify.
key_quotes: So while FY '26 included strategic investments and quarters and some quarter -specific impacts, the broader direction remains clear.
The objective is not rapid scale, but to build a credible and sustainable specialty platform over a period of time.
I would take about 100 to 150 basis points of impact coming from Pivya, from the branded business in U.S.

adds.what: F3 ophthalmic line being expanded (currently at full capacity)
F2 injectable and OSD lines: contract manufacturing and licensing in progress, expected to contribute in FY27

growth.why: Management targets low double-digit consolidated FY27 top-line growth (modelled as ~11%), with segment guides of US 10-15%, ROW 15%+, API ~10%, India near market; backing is partial, citing F3 ophthalmic expansion, F2 contract manufacturing/licensing from FY27, six Q4 US launches and Pivya, but no quantified capacity or order numbers were given for the overall guide.
